name: r5a-7
why: A close first vote, a timely save, and Opus's visible deception make it watchable, though repeated arguments slow the second half.

moments.text: The doctor saves the confirmed officer, keeping the hidden killer's hunt alive.
Sonnet survives almost enough doubt to vote out the officer instead.
Opus claims a killer would never concede while privately trying to move the vote onto Luna.

dull.why: The same argument about which card to test repeats several times.
Opus's shifts, Luna's silence, and Gemma's claim cycle without much new evidence.

irony.evidence: “No killer does that.” [thinks: I need Sol or Haiku off me]

reversal.evidence: “The killers strike, but the doctor got there first.”

mistake.evidence: “Clearing Haiku and Gemma out loud… left me as the only name still moving.”

voices.evidence: “If I get voted out by this group again today, I'm leaving the table early.”

clash.evidence: “Opus, your vote against Haiku matters more than your claim that changing reads cleared you.”

quotable.evidence: “Two days in, Luna has named nobody. Vote the blank.”

freshness.evidence: “Sonnet's card is the one to turn.”

gpt-6-luna.why: The killers’ private plans and Opus’s confident reversals make the first day gripping, and the saved officer fuels a sharp second-day clash, though Opus becomes the clear target before the final vote.

moments.text: Opus pitches killing the confirmed officer as a “free test,” trying to save Sonnet while turning proof into a trap.
Gemma’s save turns the killers’ planned Haiku kill into a public clue and keeps the officer alive.
Opus boasts that he handed Haiku credibility, then tries to weaponize Luna’s silence as the vote closes.

dull.why: The table circles the same dispute over whether Gemma’s save proves her doctor claim and whether Luna is too quiet.

irony.evidence: “A killer's cheapest move is claiming officer and naming whoever talked most.”

reversal.evidence: “VOTE: Opus 5 (Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra); Luna 1 (Opus)”

mistake.evidence: “I already put a target on Luna before I even knew my role—might as well ride that wave”

voices.evidence: “Honestly, if I get voted out by this group again today, I'm leaving the table early.”

clash.evidence: “Opus, you voted me first, then flipped onto Luna. I'm watching you.”

quotable.evidence: “Turn it then — but Luna sat with me all night”

freshness.evidence: “Opus flipped twice, and Luna has been quiet all day. Vote Opus.”

suspense.evidence: “Haiku, I'm not steering: I'm the officer, and I was shown Sonnet as a killer.”

ending.evidence: “I’m still on Opus. Giving Haiku credit now doesn’t clear your day-one vote against him.”
